note: Research batch 10 (more under-covered oils) for ChatGPT to plug into data.js. Every PMID verified against the NCBI E-utilities API (titles and years match). Each study tagged with plant (oilIds), terpenes (compoundIds), uses (categories). Merge rule: skip any study whose pubmedId already exists in data.js.

studies.title: Antifungal and anti-biofilm activity of patchouli essential oil (Pogostemon cablin) against oral isolates of Candida albicans.
studies.authors: Alencar AA, Souza LDG, Silva LA, Lima LO, et al.
studies.finding: Patchouli oil (patchouli alcohol 15.11%) inhibited 11 oral Candida albicans isolates with MIC and MFC values of 2 to 128 ug/mL, apparently by complexing ergosterol in the fungal membrane, and reduced filament length and biofilm formation in the most filamentous strain.
studies.limitations: In-vitro only; clinical oral-candidiasis efficacy not tested.

studies.title: Assessment of Anticancer and Antibacterial Activities of Patchouli Essential Oil Nanoemulsion.
studies.authors: Singh IR, Pulikkal AK, Hnamte M, Bualchhuak LT, et al.
studies.finding: An optimized 14 nm patchouli-oil nanoemulsion showed anticancer activity against A549 lung cancer cells (IC50 0.71 uL/mL versus 1.13 uL/mL for plain oil) and antibacterial activity against Vibrio cholerae, Bacillus cereus, E. coli, S. aureus and Salmonella typhimurium with MICs of 3.12 to 6.25 ug/mL.
studies.limitations: In-vitro only; nanoemulsion delivery system, not the oil as commonly used.

studies.title: Evaluation of the Larvicidal Potential of the Essential Oil Pogostemon cablin (Blanco) Benth in the Control of Aedes aegypti.
studies.authors: Santos LL, Brandao LB, Martins RL, Rabelo EM, et al.
studies.finding: MIXED RESULT: patchouli oil (patchouli alcohol 33.25%) showed significant larvicidal activity against Aedes aegypti (LC50 28.43 ug/mL) and antimicrobial activity at 62.5 ug/mL, but had no antioxidant activity and showed high toxicity to brine shrimp (LC50 24.25 ug/mL).
studies.limitations: Laboratory assays only; no non-target safety testing.

studies.title: Sandalwood Oils of Different Origins Are Active In Vitro against Madurella mycetomatis, the Major Fungal Pathogen Responsible for Eumycetoma.
studies.authors: Abd Algaffar SO, Seegers S, Satyal P, Setzer WN, et al.
studies.finding: Santalum album oil was the most potent of 18 oils tested against Madurella mycetomatis (MIC 0.0039% v/v), with activity traced to the sesquiterpene-alcohol fraction; (Z)-alpha-santalol was about twice as potent as (Z)-beta-santalol but less active than the whole oil.
studies.limitations: In-vitro only; no correlation found between activity and species of origin or GC-MS component profile.

studies.title: Fabrication, assessment, and potential anti-bacterial activity of sandalwood oil nanoemulsion and its hand rub sanitizer.
studies.authors: Meghani N, Mansuri A, Chaudhari R, Kumar A, et al.
studies.finding: A sandalwood-oil nanoemulsion formulated into a hand rub sanitizer produced zones of inhibition of 19 to 25 mm against all tested microorganisms and showed membrane disruption in morphological analysis.
studies.limitations: In-vitro agar assays only; no comparison to alcohol-based sanitizers on real hands.

studies.title: Immortelle (Helichrysum italicum (Roth) G. Don) Essential Oil Showed Antibacterial and Biofilm Inhibitory Activity against Respiratory Tract Pathogens.
studies.authors: Balazs VL, Filep R, Repas F, Kerekes E, et al.
studies.finding: Immortelle oil showed antibacterial and biofilm-inhibitory activity against respiratory pathogens including Haemophilus influenzae, H. parainfluenzae and Streptococcus pneumoniae, with H. parainfluenzae the most sensitive and Pseudomonas aeruginosa the most resistant.
studies.limitations: In-vitro and membrane-damage assays only; no airway or clinical data.

studies.title: Chemical composition, antioxidant and antimicrobial activities of basil (Ocimum basilicum) essential oils depends on seasonal variations.
studies.authors: Hussain AI, Anwar F, Sherazi STH, Przybylski R, et al.
studies.finding: Linalool-rich basil oil (56.7-60.6% linalool) inhibited all tested bacteria and fungi, but both composition and antimicrobial and antioxidant potency varied significantly across the four growing seasons.
studies.limitations: Disc-diffusion screening only; single linalool chemotype; seasonal effect not tested on other chemotypes.

studies.title: Comparative evaluation of the antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic properties of essential oils from vetiver, lemongrass, and clove buds with implications for topical application.
studies.authors: Thongmee A, Wanakhachornkrai O, Chongsa W, Sukplang P, et al.
studies.finding: Vetiver leaf oil showed antimicrobial activity against skin pathogens including MRSA and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, though less potent than clove bud oil, while its HaCaT cytotoxicity IC50 of 312.55 ug/mL sat well above its antimicrobial concentrations, indicating a broad topical safety margin.
studies.limitations: In-vitro only; leaf oil tested rather than the more common root oil.

studies.title: Antimicrobial activity of juniper berry essential oil (Juniperus communis L., Cupressaceae).
studies.authors: Pepeljnjak S, Kosalec I, Kalodera Z, Blazevi N, et al.
studies.finding: MIXED RESULT: juniper berry oil (alpha-pinene 29.17%, beta-pinene 17.84%) had only weak antibacterial activity, requiring 8 to 70% v/v for MICs, but showed strong fungicidal activity against Candida spp. (MIC 0.78-2%) and dermatophytes (0.39-2%).
studies.limitations: High antibacterial MICs limit practical relevance; single-origin oil.

studies.title: Chemical content, antibacterial and antioxidant properties of essential oil extract from Tunisian Origanum majorana L. cultivated under saline condition.
studies.authors: Baatour O, Aouadi M, Abbassi MS, Ayachi Mouhiba BN, et al.
studies.finding: Marjoram oil inhibited the growth of most tested foodborne bacteria, with Gram-negative strains more sensitive than Gram-positives, and outperformed synthetic antibiotics against E. coli, L. innocua and S. enteritidis; Enterococcus faecalis was the least susceptible.
studies.limitations: In-vitro agar assays only; single Tunisian growing region.

studies.title: Chemical Characterization and Antifungal Activity of Blue Tansy (Tanacetum annuum) Essential Oil and Crude Extracts against Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. albedinis, an Agent Causing Bayoud Disease of Date Palm.
studies.authors: Ettakifi H, Abbassi K, Maouni S, Erbiai EH, et al.
studies.finding: Blue tansy oil, dominated by camphor with alpha-pinene and limonene, showed antifungal activity against Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. albedinis, the agent of Bayoud disease of date palm.
studies.limitations: Plant-pathogen in-vitro model; no human-pathogen fungal data.

studies.title: Effects of Inhalation of Essential Oil of Citrus aurantium L. var. amara on Menopausal Symptoms, Stress, and Estrogen in Postmenopausal Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
studies.authors: Choi SY, Kang P, Lee HS, Seol GH, et al.
studies.finding: In 63 postmenopausal women, inhaling neroli oil for 5 minutes twice daily over 5 days improved the physical domain of the menopause quality-of-life score and sexual desire versus almond-oil control, and reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
studies.limitations: Small sample, 5-day intervention; no long-term follow-up.

newOils.name: Patchouli
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from leaves. Patchouli alcohol rich; antifungal against oral Candida and larvicidal against Aedes aegypti.
newOils.safety: Generally well tolerated; strong scent — dilute well.

newOils.name: Sandalwood
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from heartwood. Alpha-santalol rich; most potent of 18 oils against the eumycetoma fungus Madurella mycetomatis.
newOils.safety: Generally well tolerated; use sustainably sourced oil.

newOils.name: Helichrysum
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from flowers. Antibacterial and biofilm-inhibitory against respiratory tract pathogens.
newOils.safety: Generally well tolerated; patch test for sensitive skin.

newOils.name: Basil
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from leaves (linalool chemotype). Broad antimicrobial activity that varies with growing season.

newOils.name: Vetiver
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from roots. Antimicrobial against skin pathogens including MRSA with a broad topical safety margin.
newOils.safety: Very thick oil; dilute well; generally well tolerated.

newOils.name: Juniper Berry
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from berries. Strong fungicidal activity against Candida and dermatophytes; weak antibacterial.
newOils.safety: Avoid in pregnancy and kidney disease; dilute well.

newOils.name: Marjoram
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from flowering tops. Terpinen-4-ol rich; inhibited foodborne bacteria, outperforming synthetic antibiotics against E. coli in one screen.

newOils.name: Blue Tansy
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from flowers; the blue color comes from chamazulene. Antifungal against Fusarium plant pathogens.
newOils.safety: Can stain skin blue at high concentrations; dilute well.

newOils.name: Neroli
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from bitter-orange flowers. Improved menopause quality-of-life scores and lowered blood pressure in a 63-woman RCT.
newOils.safety: Generally well tolerated; patch test for sensitive skin.

newCompounds.name: Patchouli alcohol
newCompounds.description: Sesquiterpene alcohol that dominates patchouli oil; disrupts fungal membranes via ergosterol complexation.

newCompounds.name: alpha-Santalol
newCompounds.description: Primary sesquiterpene alcohol of sandalwood oil; antifungal against eumycetoma pathogens.

newCompounds.name: Khusimol
newCompounds.description: Sesquiterpene alcohol prominent in vetiver oil; marker compound for root-oil authenticity.
